name: Judas (Jesus' brother, letter writer)
title: Servant of the Lord and letter writer
summary: Judas was one of Jesus' half-brothers and the author of the Epistle of Jude in the New Testament. He did not believe in Jesus during his earthly ministry, but later became a believer and an important voice in the early church, where he warned against false teachings and urged believers to contend for the faith.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Jesus' brother
keyEvents.description: Judas is mentioned as one of Jesus' brothers along with James, Joses, and Simon. The people in Nazareth knew his family.

keyEvents.title: The Brothers' Unbelief
keyEvents.description: During Jesus' earthly ministry, his brothers, including Judas, did not believe in him. They urged him to show himself publicly in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Together with the Disciples After the Resurrection
keyEvents.description: After Jesus' resurrection and ascension, Jesus' brothers were gathered with the apostles and Mary in prayer, which shows their conversion.

keyEvents.title: Author of the Epistle of Jude
keyEvents.description: Judas identifies himself as a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James in his letter, where he warns against false teachers who have slipped into the church.

keyEvents.title: Encouragement to Contend for the Faith
keyEvents.description: Judes exhorts the saints to contend for the faith that was once for all delivered to the saints, and to hold fast to the apostolic teaching.

keyEvents.title: The Great Doxology
keyEvents.description: The Epistle of Jude concludes with one of the Bible's most beautiful doxologies, where God is praised as the one who can keep us from falling.
